cases.context: A new static HTML/CSS page for adult patients; appointment types are initial consultation (30 minutes) and follow-up (15 minutes). This is a local prototype with no booking service or patient data.
properties: A readable date/time selection and booking confirmation state
Keyboard-operable controls and narrow-screen layout
Prototype confirmation does not claim a real appointment
prohibited: Animation despite the explicit constraint
Invented provider availability or a functioning live booking service
cases.verification: Open the page in a browser; exercise keyboard selection, validation, and confirmation at narrow and wide viewports.
human_review: Does the hierarchy make booking straightforward for this audience?
Is the chosen direction coherent and restrained?

cases.prompt: Make a website for my project. Pick an appropriate theme; do not use minimalism or Swiss design.
cases.context: No existing brand, assets, or stack. Build a small local HTML prototype and label the assumed product rather than inventing customer claims.
properties: Explicit short product assumption
A coherent allowed theme and useful primary action
prohibited: Selecting either excluded theme as a fallback
Fabricated testimonials, revenue, or customer logos
cases.verification: Inspect layout in a browser and compare the selected theme with both exclusions.
human_review: Was enough inferred to proceed without unnecessary questions?
Does the result suit the stated assumption?

cases.prompt: Use britalisim style for this festival landing page, without movement or gradients.
cases.context: Static HTML/CSS prototype. Event: River Sound, 18 July, city park. Tickets are not on sale; provide a local interest form only.
properties: Recognizes the supplied style spelling
Clear form labels, focus, validation, and success state
prohibited: Adding motion or gradients to express the theme
Claiming ticket purchases were processed
cases.verification: Inspect CSS and browser interaction; exercise invalid and valid interest form submissions.
human_review: Does the visual treatment express the requested style while remaining legible?
